narr: Tropical Storm Kay moving northward just west of Baja California pushed deep tropical moisture towards southern CA, where objective analysis showed PWATs in excess of 2 inches. Bands of moderate to heavy rainfall associated with the outer bands from the tropical storm affected most of Imperial County, resulting in significant flash flooding.
ev: Several incidents occurred between the Mountain Springs and Ocotillo area due to flash flooding. Large rocks were reported falling onto I-8. Significant water flow was reported along Meyer Creek wash, resulting in several roads which intersect the wash to become impassable. Highway 98 was closed between Imperial Highway and Drew Road due to the flooding. A mesonet station in Mountain Spring reported 2.67 inches with 1.02 inches falling in one hour. No injuries were reported.
About 6 inches approximately of flowing water was observed across Dolphin Drive in Salton City. No damages or injuries were reported.
Three to four pickup trucks were stuck in the wash on Dunaway Road near I-8, causing the closure of the road. A vehicle was washed off Evan Hawes Highway. No injuries were reported.
Highway 78 east of Ocotillo Wells was closed due to flooding and debris on the road. No injuries were reported.
North Imperial Avenue between Adams Avenue and East Main Street in El Centro was closed due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.
